procedures.description: Use when the user asks what Cantor means, is, represents, or governs. Retrieve its signed SOP definition before answering. Do not use for a supplied identity-conflict claim or a before/after transition.

subject.description: The SOP subject explicitly named by the user.

procedures.attention_template: Explain the resolved subject using only the verified Cantor result. Preserve fixture limitations, source attribution, uncertainty, and explicit faults.

procedures.description: Use only when the user supplies a claim and asks whether it changes, crosses, weakens, or contradicts Cantor's identity. Compare representation boundaries; do not claim external truth.

subject.description: The admitted SOP subject whose identity is being inspected.

claim.description: The caller-attributed claim to compare without silently rewriting it.

procedures.attention_template: Compare the caller-attributed claim with the verified Cantor identity. Report preserved, conflicting, unsupported, and unresolved elements. Judge representation consistency, not external truth.

procedures.description: Use only when the user supplies both an earlier attention frame and a proposed later frame. Review what the transition preserves, adds, removes, conflicts with, or leaves unresolved.

subject.description: The admitted SOP subject anchoring the transition.

after_frame.description: The caller-supplied proposed later attention frame.

procedures.attention_template: Review the before and after frames against the verified Cantor identity. Enumerate preserved, added, removed, conflicting, and unresolved elements without admitting the proposed transition.
